abstract: Protein conformational dynamics are central to biological function but remain difficult to characterise at scale. Amide hydrogen exchange (HX), measured by NMR or mass spectrometry, probes these dynamics but requires computational models for integration with structural ensembles. We benchmark models for calculating HX from ensembles using a large literature-derived dataset spanning folded and intrinsically disordered proteins. We then develop a model that identifies exchange-competent amides from local structural descriptors while accounting for electrostatic effects. The model predicts protection across a broad dynamic range in ensembles generated by molecular dynamics and generative AI. HX-guided ensemble reweighting improves agreement with independent NMR, SAXS, and folding-stability measurements. Millisecond HX distinguishes and refines alternative ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins, while reweighting of structured proteins reveals folding intermediates and low-population excited states. These results establish HX as a quantitative restraint for ensemble reweighting and provide a scalable framework for benchmarking simulations and generative protein models.
